values.value: Why the Model Context Protocol is the missing standard between AI agents and the tools they use — one integration instead of N×M adapters.
MCP is awesome: one protocol, every tool
Why the Model Context Protocol is the missing standard between AI agents and the tools they use — one integration instead of N×M adapters.

value.markup:
Every AI tool used to ship its own plugin format. Want your assistant to read files, query a database and create a calendar event? That meant three adapters, three auth flows and three sets of docs to keep in your head. Multiply that by every model and every tool and you get the N×M integration nightmare.

The Model Context Protocol fixes this by standardising the conversation. An MCP server exposes tools, resources and prompts; an MCP client — an agent, an IDE, a desktop app — connects once and speaks the same language to all of them. Write the server once and every MCP-capable client can use it. Write the client once and every server lights up.

values.value: Photo by Hal Gatewood on Unsplash
One protocol. Every tool. Zero glue code.

value.markup: That is exactly what happened on this site: an agent talked to Umbraco over MCP and modelled the schema, imported the photos, wrote the posts and published them — no backoffice clicks, no custom glue. When the protocol between minds and machines is this clean, building things gets fun again.

values.value: How an agent with MCP access went from empty Umbraco to a published blog — schema, media, content and all — in a single sitting.
MCP is awesome: content at the speed of thought
How an agent with MCP access went from empty Umbraco to a published blog — schema, media, content and all — in a single sitting.

value.markup:
Content work is where agents shine: the shape of the content is known, the words just need to be written well, and the CMS is a tool with a perfectly good API. This blog is the demo — a front page, two posts, hero images, quotes, captions — all created through the Umbraco MCP server while the site was running.

The part I love is that nothing here is bespoke. The same tools that read the content tree wrote to it: create the document types, upload the media, create the documents, publish. One protocol, one session, one sitting.

values.value: Model it. Write it. Publish it. Done.
Photo by Christopher Gower on Unsplash

value.markup: So yes — MCP is awesome. It turns a CMS into something an agent can drive as naturally as a human drives the backoffice, and it turns content work into a conversation. Try it: spin up Umbraco, point an agent at it over MCP, and ask it to build you a blog. It will.
